plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional shaded rendering of two surfaces intersecting above a labeled coordinate frame. The vertical axis rises from an origin marked 0, the y-axis runs off to the right, and the x-axis comes forward toward the lower left carrying a tick labeled 2. A downward-opening paraboloid forms a wide cap, shaded blue around its outer rim and warming to orange at the crown; a straight arrow at the upper right points to it from the label z = 4 - x squared - y squared. Rising through the cap is a vertical circular cylinder rendered in blue with a hollow open top, its wall cut off by the paraboloid so that the two meet along a closed curve high on the surface. The base of the cylinder is drawn as an ellipse lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin on one side and reaching out to the tick at 2 on the other, and a curved arrow from below points to it from the label (x - 1) squared + y squared = 1. Nesting the cylinder inside the cap makes visible exactly which portion of the paraboloid stands above the circular disk. The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.

interactions.teaches: The learner sees that the apparent overlapping surfaces form a true three-dimensional solid: a vertical cylinder clipped above by a curved paraboloid.

interactions.label: Highlight bounding part
interactions.teaches: The learner identifies which surfaces actually bound the volume and how the edge curves mark where two bounding surfaces meet.

interactions.label: Horizontal slice height z
interactions.teaches: The learner understands that each horizontal cross-section is the part of the shifted cylinder disk that still lies below the paraboloid; the slices shrink as z approaches the top.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The learner connects the xy-plane disk (x - 1)^2 + y^2 <= 1 to the three-dimensional volume obtained by lifting each base point up to z = 4 - x^2 - y^2.

interactions.label: Edit bounding equations
interactions.teaches: The learner sees how changing the upper surface or the base boundary immediately changes the enclosed solid and the integration region.

demo_steps.title: Start with the base region
demo_steps.narration: The circular disk in the xy-plane is the region (x - 1)^2 + y^2 <= 1. It is tangent to the origin and extends to x = 2 along the positive x-axis.

demo_steps.title: Lift the base to the cap
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the capped solid shows every point of the disk extruded upward until it hits z = 4 - x^2 - y^2.

demo_steps.title: Locate the cylinder wall
demo_steps.narration: The vertical wall keeps the same circular footprint at every height, but its top edge is cut by the paraboloid rather than by a flat plane.

demo_steps.title: Find the intersection curve
demo_steps.narration: The closed curve marks where the cylinder and paraboloid meet. Along this curve, both equations are true at once.

demo_steps.title: Move a horizontal slice upward
demo_steps.narration: At low height the slice nearly fills the cylinder disk. Higher up, the paraboloid level circle shrinks the allowed cross-section.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use world coordinates matching the equations. The z-axis is vertical; +x should project diagonally down-left on screen, and +y should project nearly horizontally to the right. Paraboloid: z = 4 - x^2 - y^2, draw the visible cap over x^2 + y^2 <= 4, so its base rim is radius 2 at z = 0 and its vertex is at (0,0,4). Cylinder: vertical wall over the circle (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1, radius 1 centered at (1,0), tangent to the origin and extending to x = 2. The bounded solid is {(x,y,z): (x - 1)^2 + y^2 <= 1, 0 <= z <= 4 - x^2 - y^2}. The cylinder/paraboloid intersection can be parameterized as x = 1 + cos(t), y = sin(t), z = 2 - 2cos(t), 0 <= t < 2pi. Horizontal slice at height h is the planar region satisfying (x - 1)^2 + y^2 <= 1 and x^2 + y^2 <= 4 - h. Overall scale: xy radius about 2 units, z height 4 units; axes span about x = -0.8 to 2.8, y = -2.4 to 2.8, z = 0 to 4.6. Dominant colors: translucent blue surfaces #4f9ed4 to #7eb6df, orange/red warm paraboloid crown #e9543f, pale cream inner cylinder highlight #f6ead0, dark gray/black axes and labels #111111, dashed hidden guides #777777. The paraboloid should have a blue-to-orange vertical/curvature gradient, with the warm orange concentrated near the high crown and blue along lower outer portions. The cylinder wall should be translucent blue with a pale cream highlight on the open upper-left inner rim, matching the source figure's hollow-cylinder look.
interactionPlan.notes: Render surfaces double-sided with transparency and depth sorting carefully handled. Use parametric meshes for the default equations: paraboloid as a polar grid over r in [0,2], theta in [0,2pi]; cylinder as theta samples extruded from z=0 to z=4 - x^2 - y^2 at each boundary point. For equation_input changes, sample the xy domain on a grid, extract the implicit boundary c(x,y)=0 with marching squares, fill c(x,y)<=0 where cap z>=0, and extrude vertical boundary strips up to the cap. Draw the intersection curve as a thick emissive/darker line when highlighted. Draw the slicing region as a translucent yellow or white horizontal patch with a dark outline; recompute it from the two inequalities whenever sliceHeight or equations change. Keep labels billboarded to the camera but fixed near the source positions: paraboloid label upper right with leader arrow to the orange cap, cylinder equation label below the base with leader arrow upward.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Toggle bounding surfaces: the paraboloid cap, vertical cylinder, base disk, and their intersection curves highlight one at a time, showing which surfaces enclose the volume.
- Slider for vertical slicing height: the learner moves a horizontal slice upward, the cross-section inside the cylinder appears and shrinks or grows under the paraboloid, showing how accumulated slices form the solid's volume.
- Toggle between base region and capped solid: the learner switches views, the disk (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1 highlights first and then extrudes up to z = 4 - x^2 - y^2, connecting the xy-region to the integration bounds.
- Equation input for the bounded solid: learner edits the cap z = 4 - x*x - y*y and the cylinder (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1; the cylinder wall, base disk, and paraboloid cap redraw to show the new enclosed volume.

authoredContext:
Find the volume of the solid that lies under the paraboloid z=4−x2−y2 and above the disk (x−1)2+y2=1 on the xy-plane. See the paraboloid in the figure intersecting the cylinder (x−1)2+y2=1 above the xy-plane.

Finding the volume of a solid with a paraboloid cap and a circular base.

A paraboloid with equation z = 4 minus x squared minus y squared is intersected by a cylinder with equation (x minus 1) squared + y squared = 1.

discrepancies: Initial viewpoint reverses the source's axis orientation: the source has x down-left and y to the right, while the generated view shows x toward the lower right and y toward the lower left.
A yellow horizontal slice/cross-section and highlight overlay are visible by default, but the source figure contains only the paraboloid, cylinder, axes, and equation callouts.
The generated solid appears much smaller and less textbook-like in the composition, making the cylinder/paraboloid relationship harder to recognize at a glance.
The cream-colored open top/interior of the cylinder in the source is not faithfully reproduced; the visible yellow slice reads as a different feature.
The label and leader for the paraboloid equation sit close to or over the surface rather than clearly off to the right as in the source.
evaluation.notes: The main paraboloid, shifted cylinder, axes, and equations are present, but the default camera orientation and extra yellow slice make it noticeably different from the source.
action_items: Set the initial camera/view so the x-axis points down-left and the y-axis points right, matching the reference figure.
Hide the horizontal slice and yellow highlight by default so the static view matches the textbook figure.
Increase the apparent size of the plotted solid within the canvas and place the equation callouts farther from the surfaces with clearer leader arrows.
Add or improve the cream-colored visible upper interior/rim of the cylinder instead of letting the yellow slice dominate that area.

feedback.rationale: The core concept and elements are correct, but the issues are implementation-level—camera orientation, default visibility of an extra slice, composition scale, rim styling, and label placement—so the generator should refine the rendering.

The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.

- Toggle between base region and capped solid: the learner switches views, the disk (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1 highlights first and then extrudes up to z = 4 - x^2 - y^2, connecting the xy-region to the integration bounds.
- Equation input for the bounded solid: learner edits the cap z = 4 - x*x - y*y and the cylinder (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1; the cylinder wall, base disk, and paraboloid cap redraw to show the new enclosed volume.
